text: Provide the attribute agreement study in which multiple inspectors classified the same retained boards as accept or reject against the agreed answer key.
Provide the project charter and the line's required reject-share level or improvement target.
Provide the tally of items inspectors called differently from the answer key, broken out by reject category.
Lot record in lot order: boards inspected and boards rejected per lot.
Second study on retained boards after the accept reject criteria were rewritten.
Placed and rejected counts for each placement head.
What exactly was changed when the visual accept/reject criteria were rewritten after the first retained-board study?
Was a documented assignable cause found for the unusually high-reject lot in the archived lot sequence, and if so what was it?
What documented reaction plan or ongoing control is used to sustain visual inspection agreement and respond to abnormal reject lots?
